page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-60 is a compute-optimized server instance belonging to the c2 family. It features 60 vCPUs mapped to 30 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 240.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes an L1d cache of 32 KB, an L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and an L3 cache of 24 MB. Hardware-level instruction sets include AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific memory and instruction-heavy tasks. The instance demonstrates strong read-only large block memory bandwidth at 226.55 GB/sec and write large block memory bandwidth at 97.28 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Passmark database operations and extended instructions tests also register in the strong category, scoring 22356.86 and 54838.03 respectively. Conversely, most general CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (1559.59) and multi-core (61473.27), Geekbench single-core (1317.0) and multi-core (12210.0), and Redis SET operations (53.74 million operations/sec) perform in the average range.

A notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM text generation, where the instance registers weak results, delivering 60.5 tokens/sec for a 135M model and 8.75 tokens/sec for a 7B model. However, prompt processing speeds remain in the average tier. Given the high vCPU count, dedicated allocation, and strong database and extended instruction performance, this instance is suited for compute-bound workloads, database operations, software compilation, and parallel processing tasks that do not require GPU acceleration or local NVMe storage.
